summary: God asked Jonah, 'You cared about a vine that grew overnight. Shouldn't I care about the great city of Nineveh, with 120,000 people and many animals?' The book ends with God's question. Sabbath Camp looks back at Jonah's journey.

story_reel.narration: Welcome to Sabbath Camp! God asked Jonah, 'Is it right for you to be angry about the vine?' Jonah said, 'Yes! I'm angry enough to give up!' Then God gently explained. 'You cared about this vine. You didn't plant it. You didn't make it grow. It came up in a night and died in a night. And you were upset about losing it. So shouldn't I care about Nineveh, that great city? There are more than one hundred twenty thousand people there who don't know their right hand from their left. And there are many animals too.' And that's where the book of Jonah ends: with God's question. We never hear Jonah's answer. Maybe that's because God is asking us the same question. Do we care about people the way God does? Even people who are different from us? Even people who have been mean to us? Let's remember Jonah's story. God sent Jonah to Nineveh, but he ran away. A storm came, and Jonah owned up. God sent a big fish, and Jonah prayed. God gave Jonah a second chance, and the whole city turned to God. But Jonah was grumpy about God's mercy. This week's big truth: Yahweh's love reaches everyone, even people you find hard to love. God loves them, and He can help you love them too.
